sanskrit:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला।
समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि।।
image_english: When your mind, undistracted by flowery words, remains fixed in trance, you will attain divine consciousness.
caption:
Chapter 2, Verse 53

Kṛṣṇa concludes the section on Yoga. ‘śruti-vipratipannā te’ (When your mind is no longer disturbed by the flowery language of the Vedas) and when it remains ‘niścalā’ (fixed) and ‘samādhāv acalā’ (unmoving in trance), then ‘yogam avāpsyasi’ (you will attain the divine consciousness). Currently, Arjuna is disturbed by ‘śruti’—social laws and scriptures that say ‘don’t kill elders’. Kṛṣṇa says when he transcends these relative moralities and fixes his mind solely on the Supreme Lord’s order, he will be in Samādhi. True Yoga is unwavering focus on the Absolute, disregarding public opinion or ritualistic convention.
